calls.reason: The Register's estimate from Microsoft's filing puts OpenAI's loss near $4B a month, but nothing measures LLM profits outside Nvidia. The OpenRouter study finds models are differentiated, which cuts against commoditization, so the bundle is mixed.

This causal claim is wrapped in opinion. The Bank of England says AI valuations look stretched but points to earnings, and the filings study is pre-2018. No evidence isolates the effect of hype coverage.

Anthropic's misalignment study shows failures across model families, but the claim covers every model and almost all predictions. OpenAI's structured outputs show progress in one area, so coverage is too thin to call.

Anthropic's November prompt-injection data supports the control point. But November testing found Gemini 3 Pro beating specialist clinical tools, and the reasoning and hallucination parts are not measured for that month.
The only evidence is HalluLens, which tests 13 models for hallucination. That cannot show the same failure modes across hundreds of models in every category.

The transcript shows Huang linking more compute to smarter models without mentioning AGI. Whether that counts as conflating costs with benefits is a matter of interpretation, not something the transcript can settle.
